overview.description: Wire standardised biological parts - promoters, RBSs, repressors, recombinases - into circuits that sense, compute, and actuate. Standardised assembly (MoClo / Golden Gate) makes parts composable; design tools like Cello compile Boolean logic into DNA.
objectives: design a genetic logic gate (NOT/NOR/AND) from characterised parts
predict circuit behaviour and choose reporters to characterise it
reason about load, retroactivity, and part context effects

steps.description: Pick characterised parts, compose them into a logic function, assemble the DNA with a standardised method, and characterise the transfer function with reporters.
steps.intro: A genetic circuit is a program written in DNA: repressors and promoters form gates, and standardised assembly lets you snap validated parts together predictably.

instructions.title: Specify the logic
instructions.description: Write the truth table you want (e.g. IPTG AND aTc gives GFP). Choose inputs (inducible promoters) and an output reporter.

instructions.title: Choose characterised parts
instructions.description: Select promoters, RBSs, and repressors with known strengths from a registry so behaviour is predictable.

instructions.title: Compile & assemble
instructions.description: Use Cello to map logic to a gate layout, then build with MoClo/Golden Gate hierarchical assembly.

instructions.title: Characterise
instructions.description: Measure the transfer function with reporters across input combinations; check for load and context effects, and debug part-by-part.

submission.description: Design a small genetic logic circuit, specify its parts and assembly plan, and describe the reporter experiment that would confirm the intended truth table.
